newsitem.title: USA: White House would rescind tax cuts if forecast off.
newsitem.headline: White House would rescind tax cuts if forecast off.

text.p: The White House said that if its budget and economic forecasts are wrong, it was prepared to rescind $22 billion in proposed tax cuts, and reduce spending in order to balance the budget by the 2002.
Budget director Franklin Raines said that if the estimates prove wrong, first officials would seek a "fast track" legislative process in Congress to make the needed changes.

"If that doesn't work, we are proposing sunsetting $22 billion in tax cuts as well as proposing an across-the-board reduction in spending, applying to all programs other than Social Security, of 2.25 percent," Raines said.

Raines stressed the White House felt the numbers in President Clinton's new budget proposal were accurate, but said that he also expected to have the proposal evaluated, or "scored," by the Congressional Budget Office.

The budget offers taxpayers a $98 billion tax cut over the next five years to help middle-class families with children, promote higher education and encourage savings, while seeking to eliminate the budget deficit by 2002.
The budget says the tax cuts would be partly paid for by trimming unwarranted corporate tax subsidies and extending other taxes for a total of $76 billion.
